records.completion_scope: Completed bounded historical mapped naming and ordinary corridor correspondence for the actual opening, all selected parts, upper and lower joins, Gerardo Estrada storage passage and actual selected coastal terminal. An inaccessible later project announcement leaves contemporary Santa María/Tamarindo context unverified without removing the established historical through-corridor or natural-name evidence.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative receiving-river system identity with separately named selected upper components and the mapped Gerardo Estrada impoundment. It is not one scalar name for all reaches or a statement that the complete selection is presently free-flowing.

records.region: Southern Bahia, Brazil; selected Colônia approach through Itororó and Itaju do Colônia, Cachoeira continuation through Itapé and Itabuna, and Ilhéus estuary.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected upper river is Colônia, approaching Itororó from the northwest and continuing east. Rio do Meio joins from the north farther east; Salgado joins near Itapé. Those lateral rivers are not aliases or substituted mainstems. Fundão and Santana contribute separately to the Ilhéus estuary. Barragem do Iguape is on the northern Iguape/Fundão-side drainage and is not the Colônia dam-project corridor.
records.completion_scope: Ordinary corridor-scale source correspondence covers the opening, all 40 stored parts of the single selected mainstem fragment, the Colônia course and dam-project valley, the Salgado junction, Cachoeira through Itapé/Ferradas/Itabuna, and the connected lower estuary at Ilhéus. Historical source dates and the environmental report’s project-stage status are retained. No materially missing selected through-link remains at this scale. Present operating conditions, reservoir shoreline and exact coastal endpoint are not established.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative identity of the selected Colônia–Cachoeira system. Rio Colônia is a separately named selected upper and middle reach. Cachoeira is not assigned uniformly to the upper river, impoundment, lateral tributaries or estuarine water surface.

naming_scope_details.actual_terminal_receiving_water: Connected Cachoeira–Fundão–Santana estuary at Ilhéus, opening to the Atlantic

records.completion_scope: All 50 selected parts of FID13816, including the actual Perejil opening, distinct upper Grande/Huancay reaches, meaningful tributary joins, middle Chicama bends, lower multichannel valley and actual Pacific ending, have correspondence in directly inspected independent SENAMHI originals at ordinary regional/corridor scale. No material selected through-link gap remains.

records.region: Texas, West Fork San Jacinto–Lake Conroe–Lake Houston–lower San Jacinto River corridor
records.geographic_disambiguation: Completed bounded representative San Jacinto River system identity for the selected West Fork–two-reservoir–lower-river corridor. West Fork San Jacinto River, Lake Conroe and Lake Houston remain distinct named components; the representative name is not a scalar name assigned to every reach.
records.completion_scope: Four inspected original USGSTopo views, twelve original-pixel corridor crops and a reduced lake crop establish ordinary geographic correspondence of the sole selected fragment from its western West Fork opening through all selected river reaches, Lake Conroe, both reservoir outlet settings, Lake Houston, lower San Jacinto River and actual Lynchburg–Brownwood inner tidal terminal. Original water features establish the connections; selected-model connectivity alone is not evidence. The final rendered tail cuts local shoreline and land but generalizes a continuously depicted receiving-water complex, without requiring an unestablished distinct connection. No exact bank, ultimate source, all-water straight terminal line or offshore mouth is claimed.
records.supported_name_scope: West Fork San Jacinto River for the upper and middle selected river reaches; Lake Conroe and Lake Houston for the selected reservoir passages; San Jacinto River for the lower named river and its inner tidal receiving-water setting.

scope_limits: Formal registry status, official name-transition vertices, Indigenous-name equivalence and Korean forms were not investigated.
The representative San Jacinto River identity preserves West Fork San Jacinto River and the two reservoirs as distinct named components.
The chosen opening is not an official river-source claim; the modeled length is not an official river length.

Generalized selected lines cut individual river bends, banks and reservoir-edge features. The final extension crosses local Four Corners/Lynchburg land before reaching the connected Brownwood-side tidal setting; it is not an all-water channel trace.
The actual endpoint is at the Brownwood inner tidal shoreline setting, not an outer Galveston Bay or Gulf mouth.
The original cartography establishes connected ordinary corridors, not present water levels, flow direction, dam releases, navigability or a uniform current survey.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
